results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Optional (if posting identity unknown)] [Prerequisite]: Resolve author using LINKEDIN_GET_MY_INFO; if posting as an organization, best-effort confirm eligibility using LINKEDIN_GET_COMPANY_INFO.

[Required] [Prerequisite]: Get explicit user approval for final commentary (including mentions), visibility, and lifecycleState for LINKEDIN_CREATE_LINKED_IN_POST (default to DRAFT unless publish is explicitly approved).
[Optional (if images need conversion/normalization)] [Prerequisite]: Prepare per-image bytes plus MIME type using COMPOSIO_REMOTE_WORKBENCH (avoid assumptions about local files being present).

[Required] [Prerequisite]: For each image, start upload using LINKEDIN_INITIALIZE_IMAGE_UPLOAD, then PUT bytes to the returned upload URL via COMPOSIO_REMOTE_WORKBENCH and retain the returned media reference for attachment.

[Fallback (if LINKEDIN_INITIALIZE_IMAGE_UPLOAD fails or required fields mismatch)] [Prerequisite]: Use LINKEDIN_REGISTER_IMAGE_UPLOAD per image, PUT bytes to the returned upload URL via COMPOSIO_REMOTE_WORKBENCH, and retain the returned asset reference.

[Required] [Step]: Create the multi-image post using LINKEDIN_CREATE_LINKED_IN_POST (author/visibility/lifecycleState/commentary + images[] with required per-image fields such as name/mimetype and the attachable reference); store the returned post identifier; if attachments fail validation, retry as text-only (draft/publish per approval).
[Optional (for verification/debugging)] [Next Step]: Fetch the created entity using LINKEDIN_GET_POST_CONTENT (best-effort; lack of read permission may block retrieval).
[Optional (if user approves cleanup)] [Next Step]: Remove the created post using LINKEDIN_DELETE_POST.
known_pitfalls: [LINKEDIN_GET_MY_INFO] Can return 429 (daily throttle); retries may not succeed until the service resets.
[LINKEDIN_GET_COMPANY_INFO] Can fail with 403 Forbidden when required organization-admin scopes are missing.
[LINKEDIN_CREATE_LINKED_IN_POST] Attachment validation is strict; non-resolvable images[].s3key or mismatched media references can surface as storage/download 404-style errors.
[LINKEDIN_CREATE_LINKED_IN_POST] Commentary may fail beyond ~3000 characters; can also return 422-style duplicate-content errors or 426-style version-not-active blocks.
[LINKEDIN_GET_POST_CONTENT] Can return 403 Forbidden even immediately after creation; treat verification as best-effort, not proof of failure.

reference_workbench_snippets.description: Upload image bytes to a platform-provided upload URL (out-of-band PUT) and accept common success statuses.
reference_workbench_snippets.code:
```python
import requests
resp=requests.put("<upload_url>",data=b"<bytes>",headers={"Content-Type":"image/png"},timeout=60)
print(resp.status_code)
assert resp.status_code in (200,201,204)
resp.raise_for_status()
```

reference_workbench_snippets.description: Parse LINKEDIN_REGISTER_IMAGE_UPLOAD response to extract upload URL and asset reference robustly.
reference_workbench_snippets.code:
```python
d=resp.get("data",{})
m=(d.get("upload_mechanism") or {}).get("com.linkedin.digitalmedia.uploading.MediaUploadHttpRequest",{})
upload_url=d.get("upload_url") or m.get("uploadUrl")
asset_ref=d.get("asset_urn")
assert upload_url and asset_ref
```

LINKEDIN_CREATE_LINKED_IN_POST.description: Creates a new post on LinkedIn for the authenticated user or an organization they manage. Requires w_member_social scope for posting as a person, and w_organization_social scope for posting as an organization (with ADMINISTRATOR, DIRECT_SPONSORED_CONTENT_POSTER, or CONTENT_ADMIN role).

author.description: The URN of the LinkedIn member or organization creating the post. IMPORTANT: Replace placeholder text with actual ID values. For a person: use 'urn:li:person:<actual_person_id>' (e.g., 'urn:li:person:F6kGF1Uduq' or 'urn:li:person:123456789'). Requires w_member_social scope. For an organization: use 'urn:li:organization:<actual_org_id>' (e.g., 'urn:li:organization:987654321'). Requires w_organization_social scope and you must have ADMINISTRATOR, DIRECT_SPONSORED_CONTENT_POSTER, or CONTENT_ADMIN role for the organization. Get your person ID using the GET_MY_INFO action, or get organization IDs from GET_COMPANY_INFO. Do NOT pass literal placeholder text like '{id}' or '{organization_id}'.

name.description: The filename that will be used when uploading the file to the destination service

s3key.description: The S3 key of a publicly accessible file, typically returned from a previous download action that stored the file in S3. This key references an existing file that can be uploaded to another service.

mimetype.description: The MIME type of the file

images.description: Array of images to upload and attach to the post. Each element is a Supports 1-20 images. For a single image, use a list with one element. LinkedIn will automatically use the appropriate content type (media for single image, multiImage for 2+ images).

container.description: Container entity URN for posting within a specific container (e.g., 'urn:li:group:123456' for group posts). Use this field when posting to a group or other container entity.

examples: Excited to share our new product update!
commentary.description: The main text content of the post. This field supports plain text and @-mentions (e.g., @[LinkedIn Member](urn:li:person:xxxx)). Maximum length: 3000 characters.

visibility.description: Controls who can see the post. 'PUBLIC' makes it visible to everyone, 'CONNECTIONS' to connections only, 'LOGGED_IN' to signed-in LinkedIn members, and 'CONTAINER' for specific group/event posts.

degrees.description: Array of standardized degree URNs for targeting.

locations.description: Deprecated. Array of location URNs for targeting. Use geoLocations instead.

industries.description: Array of industry URNs for targeting.

seniorities.description: Array of seniority level URNs for targeting.

geoLocations.description: Array of geographic location URNs for targeting, e.g., ['urn:li:geo:103644278'].

jobFunctions.description: Array of job function URNs for targeting.

fieldsOfStudy.description: Array of field of study URNs for targeting.

organizations.description: Array of school organization URNs for targeting.

items.description: Locale object for interface language targeting.

interfaceLocales.description: Array of locale objects for interface language targeting.

items.description: Organization staff count range for targeting.

staffCountRanges.description: Array of organization staff count ranges for targeting.

items.description: Targeting criteria for post distribution. The targeted audience must be greater than 300 members.

targetEntities.description: Array of targeting criteria objects. Each object can specify geoLocations, degrees, industries, seniorities, etc. The targeted audience must be greater than 300 members.

feedDistribution.description: Specifies how the post is distributed on the LinkedIn feed. 'MAIN_FEED' distributes to the main feed, 'NONE' creates Direct Sponsored Content and requires adContext.dscAdAccount.

thirdPartyDistributionChannels.description: Array of third-party channels where the post should be distributed, e.g., Twitter.

distribution.description: Specifies distribution rules for the post, including feed distribution and targeting.

lifecycleState.description: The state of the post. Use 'PUBLISHED' to post directly, 'DRAFT' to save as a draft, or 'PUBLISH_REQUESTED' if the post requires review before publishing.

parent.description: URN of the post being reshared (e.g., 'urn:li:share:6844785523593134080' or 'urn:li:ugcPost:6844785523593134080').

contentLandingPage.description: URL of the landing page that opens when the call-to-action button is clicked. Optional even when contentCallToActionLabel is set.

isReshareDisabledByAuthor.description: Set to true to prevent others from resharing this post.

LINKEDIN_GET_MY_INFO.description: Fetches the authenticated LinkedIn user's profile information including name, headline, profile picture, and other profile details.

LINKEDIN_INITIALIZE_IMAGE_UPLOAD.description: Tool to initialize an image upload to LinkedIn and return a presigned upload URL plus the resulting image URN. Use when you need to prepare an image upload for LinkedIn posts. After calling this tool, upload the image bytes to the returned upload_url via PUT request, then use the image URN in CREATE_LINKED_IN_POST action.

owner.description: Owner URN (person or organization) that will own the uploaded image. Must be in the format 'urn:li:person:{id}' for personal posts or 'urn:li:organization:{id}' for organization posts. Use the GET_MY_INFO action to retrieve the person ID.
